name: TinyHumans SDK source release
# TinyBus is the loader/runtime SDK, not a loadable module: it has no cdylib.
# Its source archive is intentional; 17 native module archives do not apply.
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      tag:
        type: string
        required: true
      version:
        type: string
        required: true
      package:
        type: string
        required: true
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  package:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.tag }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          submodules: recursive
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@686976e191b89faba57d3206551f0f330d8cb249
      - name: Validate and package reviewed SDK source
        env:
          PACKAGE: ${{ inputs.package }}
          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          [[ "$PACKAGE" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ ]]
          [[ "$VERSION" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([+-][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]
          git fetch origin main
          git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main
          actual="$(cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 | jq -er --arg name "$PACKAGE" '.packages[] | select(.name == $name) | .version')"
          [[ "$actual" == "$VERSION" ]]
          cargo test --locked --workspace --all-features
          mkdir -p release-assets
          archive="$PACKAGE-$VERSION-source.tar.gz"
          git archive --format=tar.gz --prefix="$PACKAGE-$VERSION/" HEAD > "release-assets/$archive"
          hash="$(sha256sum "release-assets/$archive" | cut -d ' ' -f 1)"
          printf '"%s" = "%s"\n' "$archive" "$hash" > release-assets/checksum.toml
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@65462800fd760344b1a7b4382951275a0abb4808
        with:
          name: sdk-release-assets
          path: release-assets/*
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: package
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093
        with:
          name: sdk-release-assets
          path: release-assets
      - name: Verify and publish immutable SDK release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
          PACKAGE: ${{ inputs.package }}
          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          [[ "$PACKAGE" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ ]]
          [[ "$VERSION" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([+-][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]
          archive="$PACKAGE-$VERSION-source.tar.gz"
          expected_files=$'checksum.toml\n'"$archive"
          actual_files="$(find release-assets -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type f -printf '%f\n' | sort)"
          if [[ "$(find release-assets -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -type f -print -quit)" != "" || "$actual_files" != "$(printf '%s\n' "$expected_files" | sort)" ]]; then
            echo "downloaded SDK artifact has an unexpected file set" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          digest="$(sha256sum "release-assets/$archive" | awk '{print $1}')"
          [[ "$(cat release-assets/checksum.toml)" == "\"$archive\" = \"$digest\"" ]]
          release_type=()
          if [[ "${VERSION%%+*}" == *-* ]]; then release_type+=(--prerelease); fi
          if gh release view "$TAG" --json assets >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            release="$(gh release view "$TAG" --json assets,isDraft,isPrerelease)"
            is_draft="$(jq -r '.isDraft' <<<"$release")"
            is_prerelease="$(jq -r '.isPrerelease' <<<"$release")"
            existing="$(jq -r '.assets[].name' <<<"$release" | sort)"
            expected="$(printf '%s\n' checksum.toml "$archive" | sort)"
            [[ "$existing" == "$expected" ]] || { echo "release $TAG has a different asset set" >&2; exit 1; }
            existing_assets="$(mktemp -d "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/sdk-release-assets.XXXXXX")"
            gh release download "$TAG" --dir "$existing_assets" --clobber
            for name in checksum.toml "$archive"; do
              expected_digest="$(sha256sum "release-assets/$name" | awk '{print $1}')"
              actual_digest="$(sha256sum "$existing_assets/$name" | awk '{print $1}')"
              [[ "$expected_digest" == "$actual_digest" ]] || { echo "release $TAG asset $name has different contents" >&2; exit 1; }
            done
            rm -rf "$existing_assets"
            expected_prerelease=false
            if [[ ${#release_type[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then expected_prerelease=true; fi
            [[ "$is_prerelease" == "$expected_prerelease" ]] || { echo "release $TAG has the wrong prerelease state" >&2; exit 1; }
            if [[ "$is_draft" == true ]]; then
              gh release edit "$TAG" --draft=false "${release_type[@]}"
              echo "published verified draft release $TAG"
            else
              echo "release $TAG already exists with verified asset contents; skipping retry"
            fi
          else
            flags=(--verify-tag --title "$TAG")
            if [[ ${#release_type[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then flags+=(--prerelease); fi
            gh release create "$TAG" release-assets/* "${flags[@]}"
          fi

# Builds ghcr.io/tinyhumansai/rust_ci from images/rust-ci/Dockerfile: the
# toolbox Rust workspaces run their CI jobs in (`container:`). Pull requests
# build it without pushing; main pushes it whenever its inputs change.
name: Rust CI image
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - images/rust-ci/**
      - .github/workflows/rust-ci-image.yml
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - images/rust-ci/**
      - .github/workflows/rust-ci-image.yml
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write
concurrency:
  group: rust-ci-image-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Read the image's Rust version
        id: meta
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rust="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RUST_STABLE=//p' images/rust-ci/Dockerfile)"
          [ -n "${rust}" ] || { echo "no ARG RUST_STABLE in the Dockerfile" >&2; exit 1; }
          echo "rust=${rust}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
        with:
          context: images/rust-ci
          push: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}
          provenance: false
          # The sha tag names the commit `latest` was built from; pin it.
          tags: |-
            ghcr.io/tinyhumansai/rust_ci:latest
            ghcr.io/tinyhumansai/rust_ci:rust-${{ steps.meta.outputs.rust }}
            ghcr.io/tinyhumansai/rust_ci:sha-${{ github.sha }}

name: TinyHumans module CI

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      coverage-script:
        description: Repository-relative Bash script that enforces the shared per-file coverage threshold.
        type: string
        required: true
      msrv:
        description: Deprecated compatibility input; MSRV is read from Cargo.toml.
        type: string
        default: ''
      msrv-build-targets:
        description: Optional validated Cargo build groups for the declared MSRV.
        type: string
        default: ''
      module-e2e-script:
        description: Repository-relative Bash script that runs the module loader end-to-end suite.
        type: string
        required: true
      module-e2e-toolchain:
        description: "Compiler for module E2E: declared, stable, or an exact Rust version such as 1.88.0."
        type: string
        default: declared
      feature-test-script:
        description: Repository-relative Bash script that runs the module's feature-level test suite.
        type: string
        required: true
      apt-packages:
        description: Additional Ubuntu packages required by the module.
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  fmt:
    name: fmt
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          submodules: recursive
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@686976e191b89faba57d3206551f0f330d8cb249 # stable as of 2026-10-10
        with:
          components: rustfmt
      - run: cargo fmt --all -- --check

  clippy:
    name: clippy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          submodules: recursive
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@686976e191b89faba57d3206551f0f330d8cb249 # stable as of 2026-10-10
        with:
          components: clippy
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
      - if: inputs.apt-packages != ''
        shell: bash
        env:
          APT_PACKAGES: ${{ inputs.apt-packages }}
        run: |
          [[ "$APT_PACKAGES" =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9+.-]*(:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)?([ ][a-z0-9][a-z0-9+.-]*(:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)?)*$ ]] || {
            echo "apt-packages must be a space-separated list of package names" >&2
            exit 2
          }
          read -r -a packages <<< "$APT_PACKAGES"
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install --yes "${packages[@]}"
      - run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

  test:
    name: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          submodules: recursive
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@686976e191b89faba57d3206551f0f330d8cb249 # stable as of 2026-10-10
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
      - if: inputs.apt-packages != ''
        shell: bash
        env:
          APT_PACKAGES: ${{ inputs.apt-packages }}
        run: |
          [[ "$APT_PACKAGES" =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9+.-]*(:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)?([ ][a-z0-9][a-z0-9+.-]*(:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)?)*$ ]] || {
            echo "apt-packages must be a space-separated list of package names" >&2
            exit 2
          }
          read -r -a packages <<< "$APT_PACKAGES"
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install --yes "${packages[@]}"
      - run: cargo test --workspace

  coverage:
    name: coverage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          submodules: recursive
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@686976e191b89faba57d3206551f0f330d8cb249 # stable as of 2026-10-10
        with:
          components: llvm-tools-preview
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@70b10d055da4af0e46b2f7166e710204993798b3 # immutable revision
        with:
          tool: cargo-llvm-cov
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
      - if: inputs.apt-packages != ''
        shell: bash
        env:
          APT_PACKAGES: ${{ inputs.apt-packages }}
        run: |
          [[ "$APT_PACKAGES" =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9+.-]*(:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)?([ ][a-z0-9][a-z0-9+.-]*(:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)?)*$ ]] || {
            echo "apt-packages must be a space-separated list of package names" >&2
            exit 2
          }
          read -r -a packages <<< "$APT_PACKAGES"
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install --yes "${packages[@]}"
      - name: Enforce the per-file coverage threshold
        shell: bash
        env:
          COVERAGE_SCRIPT: ${{ inputs.coverage-script }}
        run: |
          [[ "$COVERAGE_SCRIPT" =~ ^scripts/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+\.sh$ && "$COVERAGE_SCRIPT" != */../* && "$COVERAGE_SCRIPT" != scripts/../* ]] || {
            echo "coverage-script must name a repository-local scripts/*.sh file" >&2
            exit 2
          }
          [[ -f "$COVERAGE_SCRIPT" ]] || { echo "coverage script is missing: $COVERAGE_SCRIPT" >&2; exit 2; }
          bash "$COVERAGE_SCRIPT"

  docs:
    name: docs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          submodules: recursive
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@686976e191b89faba57d3206551f0f330d8cb249 # stable as of 2026-10-10
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
      - if: inputs.apt-packages != ''
        shell: bash
        env:
          APT_PACKAGES: ${{ inputs.apt-packages }}
        run: |
          [[ "$APT_PACKAGES" =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9+.-]*(:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)?([ ][a-z0-9][a-z0-9+.-]*(:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)?)*$ ]] || {
            echo "apt-packages must be a space-separated list of package names" >&2
            exit 2
          }
          read -r -a packages <<< "$APT_PACKAGES"
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install --yes "${packages[@]}"
      - run: cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps
        env:
          RUSTDOCFLAGS: -D warnings

  msrv:
    name: msrv
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          submodules: recursive
      - id: msrv
        shell: bash
        run: |
          version="$(cargo metadata --format-version 1 --quiet | jq -er '
            . as $metadata
            | .resolve.root as $root
            | if $root != null then
                ([.packages[] | select(.id == $root) | .rust_version] | first) as $version
                | if ($version | type) != "string" then
                    error("workspace root package must declare rust-version")
                  elif ($version | test("^[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$")) then
                    $version
                  else
                    error("workspace root rust-version must be numeric X.Y or X.Y.Z")
                  end
              else
                [.packages[]
                  | select(.id as $id | $metadata.workspace_members | index($id))
                  | .rust_version
                  | select(. != null)] as $versions
                | if ($versions | length) == 0 then
                    error("workspace members must declare rust-version")
                  elif any($versions[]; (type != "string") or (test("^[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$") | not)) then
                    error("workspace package rust-version must be numeric X.Y or X.Y.Z")
                  else
                    [$versions[] | {version: ., parts: (split(".") | map(tonumber))}]
                    | max_by(.parts)
                    | .version
                  end
              end
          ')"
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@e2a55d2ffb04f378e9626c28d38b36d230d1e12f # master as of 2026-10-10
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.msrv.outputs.version }}
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
      - if: inputs.apt-packages != ''
        shell: bash
        env:
          APT_PACKAGES: ${{ inputs.apt-packages }}
        run: |
          [[ "$APT_PACKAGES" =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9+.-]*(:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)?([ ][a-z0-9][a-z0-9+.-]*(:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)?)*$ ]] || {
            echo "apt-packages must be a space-separated list of package names" >&2
            exit 2
          }
          read -r -a packages <<< "$APT_PACKAGES"
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install --yes "${packages[@]}"
      - name: Build with the declared MSRV
        shell: bash
        env:
          MSRV_BUILD_TARGETS: ${{ inputs.msrv-build-targets }}
        run: |
          if [[ -z "$MSRV_BUILD_TARGETS" ]]; then
            cargo build --workspace --all-targets --all-features
            exit
          fi
          jq -e '
            type == "array" and length > 0 and all(.[];
              (.packages | type == "array" and length > 0 and all(.[]; type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$"))) and
              ((.features // []) | type == "array" and all(.[]; type == "string" and test("^(dep:[A-Za-z0-9_-]+|[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(\\??/[A-Za-z0-9_.+-]+)?|[A-Za-z0-9_.+-]+)$"))) and
              ((.all_targets // false) | type == "boolean") and
              ((.all_features // false) | type == "boolean") and
              ((.no_default_features // false) | type == "boolean")
            )
          ' <<< "$MSRV_BUILD_TARGETS" >/dev/null
          while IFS= read -r target; do
            metadata="$(cargo +stable metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps)"
            while IFS= read -r feature; do
              if [[ "$feature" != */* ]] && ! jq -e --arg feature "$feature" --argjson names "$(jq '.packages' <<< "$target")" '
                any(.packages[]; (.name as $name | $names | index($name)) != null and ((.features // {}) | has($feature)))
              ' <<< "$metadata" >/dev/null; then
                echo "feature $feature is not declared by any selected package" >&2
                exit 2
              fi
            done < <(jq -r '.features[]?' <<< "$target")
            while IFS= read -r package; do
              version="$(jq -er --arg name "$package" '.packages[] | select(.name == $name) | .rust_version // error("package must declare rust-version")' <<< "$metadata")"
              rustup toolchain install "$version" --profile minimal
              # Replace the group's package list with the package being checked.
              package_args=(--package "$package")
              while IFS= read -r feature; do
                prefix="${feature%%/*}"
                if [[ "$feature" == */* && "$prefix" != "$package" ]] &&
                  jq -e --arg prefix "$prefix" '.packages | index($prefix) != null' <<< "$target" >/dev/null; then
                  continue
                fi
                if [[ "$feature" != */* ]] && ! jq -e --arg name "$package" --arg feature "$feature" '
                  .packages[] | select(.name == $name) | (.features // {}) | has($feature)
                ' <<< "$metadata" >/dev/null; then
                  continue
                fi
                package_args+=(--features "$feature")
              done < <(jq -r '.features[]?' <<< "$target")
              [[ "$(jq -r '.all_targets // false' <<< "$target")" == true ]] && package_args+=(--all-targets)
              [[ "$(jq -r '.all_features // false' <<< "$target")" == true ]] && package_args+=(--all-features)
              [[ "$(jq -r '.no_default_features // false' <<< "$target")" == true ]] && package_args+=(--no-default-features)
              cargo "+$version" build "${package_args[@]}"
            done < <(jq -r '.packages[]' <<< "$target")
          done < <(jq -c '.[]' <<< "$MSRV_BUILD_TARGETS")

  supply-chain:
    name: supply-chain
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          submodules: recursive
      - uses: EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@9c67a826e39827395bfa619cd85cb2aaeb43cfaa # immutable revision

  module-e2e:
    name: module-e2e (${{ matrix.os }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          submodules: recursive
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@686976e191b89faba57d3206551f0f330d8cb249 # stable as of 2026-10-10
      - id: msrv
        shell: bash
        run: |
          version="$(cargo metadata --format-version 1 --quiet | jq -er '
            . as $metadata
            | .resolve.root as $root
            | if $root != null then
                ([.packages[] | select(.id == $root) | .rust_version] | first) as $version
                | if ($version | type) != "string" then
                    error("workspace root package must declare rust-version")
                  elif ($version | test("^[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$")) then
                    $version
                  else
                    error("workspace root rust-version must be numeric X.Y or X.Y.Z")
                  end
              else
                [.packages[]
                  | select(.id as $id | $metadata.workspace_members | index($id))
                  | .rust_version
                  | select(. != null)] as $versions
                | if ($versions | length) == 0 then
                    error("workspace members must declare rust-version")
                  elif any($versions[]; (type != "string") or (test("^[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$") | not)) then
                    error("workspace package rust-version must be numeric X.Y or X.Y.Z")
                  else
                    [$versions[] | {version: ., parts: (split(".") | map(tonumber))}]
                    | max_by(.parts)
                    | .version
                  end
              end
          ')"
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@e2a55d2ffb04f378e9626c28d38b36d230d1e12f # master as of 2026-10-10
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.msrv.outputs.version }}
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
      - if: runner.os == 'Linux' && inputs.apt-packages != ''
        shell: bash
        env:
          APT_PACKAGES: ${{ inputs.apt-packages }}
        run: |
          [[ "$APT_PACKAGES" =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9+.-]*(:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)?([ ][a-z0-9][a-z0-9+.-]*(:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)?)*$ ]] || {
            echo "apt-packages must be a space-separated list of package names" >&2
            exit 2
          }
          read -r -a packages <<< "$APT_PACKAGES"
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install --yes "${packages[@]}"
      - name: Select the module E2E toolchain
        shell: bash
        env:
          MODULE_E2E_TOOLCHAIN: ${{ inputs.module-e2e-toolchain }}
        run: |
          case "$MODULE_E2E_TOOLCHAIN" in
            declared) ;;
            stable) rustup override set stable ;;
            *)
              [[ "$MODULE_E2E_TOOLCHAIN" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]] || {
                echo "module-e2e-toolchain must be 'declared', 'stable', or an exact X.Y.Z version" >&2
                exit 2
              }
              rustup toolchain install "$MODULE_E2E_TOOLCHAIN" --profile minimal
              rustup override set "$MODULE_E2E_TOOLCHAIN"
              ;;
          esac
      - shell: bash
        env:
          MODULE_E2E_SCRIPT: ${{ inputs.module-e2e-script }}
        run: |
          [[ "$MODULE_E2E_SCRIPT" =~ ^scripts/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+\.sh$ && "$MODULE_E2E_SCRIPT" != */../* && "$MODULE_E2E_SCRIPT" != scripts/../* ]] || {
            echo "module-e2e-script must name a repository-local scripts/*.sh file" >&2
            exit 2
          }
          [[ -f "$MODULE_E2E_SCRIPT" ]] || { echo "module E2E script is missing: $MODULE_E2E_SCRIPT" >&2; exit 2; }
          bash "$MODULE_E2E_SCRIPT"

  feature-tests:
    name: feature-tests (${{ matrix.os }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          submodules: recursive
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@686976e191b89faba57d3206551f0f330d8cb249 # stable as of 2026-10-10
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
      - if: runner.os == 'Linux' && inputs.apt-packages != ''
        shell: bash
        env:
          APT_PACKAGES: ${{ inputs.apt-packages }}
        run: |
          [[ "$APT_PACKAGES" =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9+.-]*(:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)?([ ][a-z0-9][a-z0-9+.-]*(:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)?)*$ ]] || {
            echo "apt-packages must be a space-separated list of package names" >&2
            exit 2
          }
          read -r -a packages <<< "$APT_PACKAGES"
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install --yes "${packages[@]}"
      - shell: bash
        env:
          FEATURE_TEST_SCRIPT: ${{ inputs.feature-test-script }}
        run: |
          [[ "$FEATURE_TEST_SCRIPT" =~ ^scripts/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+\.sh$ && "$FEATURE_TEST_SCRIPT" != */../* && "$FEATURE_TEST_SCRIPT" != scripts/../* ]] || {
            echo "feature-test-script must name a repository-local scripts/*.sh file" >&2
            exit 2
          }
          [[ -f "$FEATURE_TEST_SCRIPT" ]] || { echo "feature test script is missing: $FEATURE_TEST_SCRIPT" >&2; exit 2; }
          bash "$FEATURE_TEST_SCRIPT"

# Checkout with selective submodules

`actions/checkout` with `submodules: recursive` clones every submodule, one
at a time. For a repository that vendors OpenHuman, that is roughly 70 clones
and a minute of every job, wiki submodules included, though no build reads
them.

This action checks the repository out with `actions/checkout` (submodules off)
and then adds the submodules itself:

- **shallow**: `submodule-depth`, 1 by default;
- **in parallel**: every parent of a level updates at once, each cloning
  `jobs` submodules at a time;
- **selectively**: a submodule whose path matches `exclude-submodules` is left
  as an empty directory, and nothing beneath it is visited.

```yaml
- uses: tinyhumansai/.github/actions/checkout@<sha>
  with:
    exclude-submodules: |
      wiki
      vendor/openhuman/app
```

A pattern is a bash glob over the submodule's path from the repository root,
where `*` also matches `/`. A pattern without a `/` matches the last path
component at any depth, so the default `wiki` leaves out every submodule
named `wiki`.

Measured from a laptop on openhuman's 51 nested submodules:
`git submodule update --init --recursive --depth 1` took 163s, and this
action's script took 62s (46 cloned, 5 wikis skipped).

## Credentials

`token` (default `github.token`) is sent to github.com as an HTTP header via
`GIT_CONFIG_*` environment variables that only the submodule step sees. It is
never written to a git config. `persist-credentials` defaults to `false`,
unlike `actions/checkout`, because CI jobs that build repository code should
not keep a token in `.git/config`.

## Container jobs

In a `container:` job git runs as root over a workspace the runner's user
owns, and refuses it as unsafe. The submodule step sets `safe.directory=*`
for its own git calls, the same way, through the environment. Later steps
that run git in the workspace need
`git config --global --add safe.directory "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` themselves.

The tests are in `scripts/test-checkout-submodules.py`.

# rust_ci image

`ghcr.io/tinyhumansai/rust_ci` holds what a Rust workspace's CI job would
otherwise install step by step, so the job starts at its first cargo
command:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| Ubuntu | 22.04 (the same base as `openhuman_ci` and the EX63 guest) |
| Rust | `stable` (1.99.1) with rustfmt, clippy, llvm-tools; `1.96` (MSRV); `nightly-2026-10-14` with the Cranelift backend |
| cargo-llvm-cov, cargo-deny | 0.9.1, 0.20.2 |
| tinymold | 0.2.0 |
| MongoDB server, mongosh | 7.0.45, latest 2.x |
| mold, clang, cmake, libssl-dev, pkg-config, jq, git | Ubuntu's |

Every downloaded binary is checked against a sha256 digest pinned in the
Dockerfile. A change to `images/rust-ci/` is built on its pull request and
pushed when it reaches main, tagged `latest`, `rust-<stable>` and
`sha-<commit>`. Pin `sha-<commit>` in workflows.

## Using it

```yaml
jobs:
  rust:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container: ghcr.io/tinyhumansai/rust_ci:sha-<commit>
    steps:
      - uses: tinyhumansai/.github/actions/checkout@<sha>
      - run: cargo test --all-features
```

Inside a container job, `services:` containers are reachable by their job
name, but `docker run` is not available. Start MongoDB in the job instead
(`mongod --fork --dbpath ... --logpath ...`). The same goes for the EX63
microVMs, which have no Docker either.

## Cranelift

The nightly carries `rustc-codegen-cranelift-preview`. Cranelift compiles
debug builds faster than LLVM and produces slower code, which is the right
trade for `cargo build` and `cargo test` in CI:

```yaml
env:
  CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_CODEGEN_BACKEND: cranelift
run: cargo +nightly-2026-10-14 -Zcodegen-backend test
```

It has no coverage instrumentation, so `cargo llvm-cov` stays on stable.
Code that panics across an `extern "C"` boundary or uses unusual SIMD
intrinsics can still hit gaps in the backend.

## Bumping

- **Rust.** Raise `RUST_STABLE` to the new stable. The build checks that
  rustup's `stable` is that version, so a stale pin fails the build rather
  than publishing a mislabeled image.
- **Nightly.** Move `RUST_NIGHTLY` to a date whose manifest still ships
  `rustc-codegen-cranelift-preview`.
- **The other tools.** Raise the version and replace its `*_SHA256` with
  the digest of the new release asset.

# otherwise install step by step. Jobs run in it with `container:`, and
# nothing is downloaded before the first cargo command.
#
# Every version is pinned here, and every binary is checked against its
# sha256 digest. Bump a version in this file, and the image is rebuilt and
# published from main (see .github/workflows/rust-ci-image.yml).
FROM ubuntu:22.04

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
    LANG=C.UTF-8

# Build tools and the native libraries the -sys crates link (openssl-sys;
# mongocrypt-sys and others build bundled sources with cc/cmake).
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        build-essential ca-certificates clang cmake curl git gnupg jq \
        libclang-dev libssl-dev mold pkg-config python3 unzip xz-utils zstd \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# MongoDB 7.0 and mongosh, for tests that need a real server

    && gpg --no-default-keyring --keyring /usr/share/keyrings/mongodb-server-7.0.gpg \
        --list-keys --with-colons | grep -q '^fpr:::::::::E58830201F7DD82CD808AA84160D26BB1785BA38:' \
    && echo "deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/mongodb-server-7.0.gpg] https://repo.mongodb.org/apt/ubuntu jammy/mongodb-org/7.0 multiverse" \
        > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/mongodb-org-7.0.list \

        "mongodb-org-server=${MONGODB_VERSION}" mongodb-mongosh \

# Rust: the stable release CI builds with, the MSRV it is checked against,
# a nightly with Cranelift, and the components clippy, fmt and cargo-llvm-cov need. Both are installed
# under the names workflows ask rustup for (`stable` and `1.96`), so
# dtolnay/rust-toolchain finds them instead of downloading them again.
ARG RUST_STABLE=1.99.1
ARG RUST_MSRV=1.96
# A dated nightly with the Cranelift codegen backend, for fast debug builds
# and tests: `cargo +nightly-... -Zcodegen-backend` with
# CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_CODEGEN_BACKEND=cranelift. Cranelift has no coverage
# instrumentation, so cargo llvm-cov stays on stable.
ARG RUST_NIGHTLY=nightly-2026-10-14
ENV RUSTUP_HOME=/usr/local/rustup \
    CARGO_HOME=/usr/local/cargo \
    PATH=/usr/local/cargo/bin:$PATH
RUN curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --no-modify-path \
        --profile minimal --default-toolchain none \
    && rustup toolchain install stable --profile minimal \
        -c rustfmt -c clippy -c llvm-tools-preview \
    && test "$(rustc +stable --version | cut -d' ' -f2)" = "${RUST_STABLE}" \
    && rustup toolchain install "${RUST_MSRV}" --profile minimal \
    && rustup toolchain install "${RUST_NIGHTLY}" --profile minimal \
        -c rustc-codegen-cranelift-preview -c clippy -c rustfmt \
    && rustup default stable \
    && chmod -R a+w "${RUSTUP_HOME}" "${CARGO_HOME}"

# Cargo tools, as release binaries checked against pinned digests.
ARG CARGO_LLVM_COV_VERSION=0.9.1
ARG CARGO_LLVM_COV_SHA256=b3f68e625481fed9b16444174f3fa5ebcdbde4a1878803a35eabe2dcefcdc41a
ARG CARGO_DENY_VERSION=0.20.2
ARG CARGO_DENY_SHA256=9f12ed4c49936e09b48bf862b595cde2fe64fcbd9d74dfacac6131ca824c8d5f
ARG TINYMOLD_VERSION=0.2.0
ARG TINYMOLD_SHA256=cccb75cdeccf29b3647832c5c7b3d5dc515f32cf07a9aba139e983ffb977fc4d
RUN set -eu; dl="$(mktemp -d)"; \
    fetch() { curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "${dl}/$1" "$2" && echo "$3  ${dl}/$1" | sha256sum -c --quiet -; }; \
    fetch llvm-cov.tgz "https://github.com/taiki-e/cargo-llvm-cov/releases/download/v${CARGO_LLVM_COV_VERSION}/cargo-llvm-cov-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz" "${CARGO_LLVM_COV_SHA256}"; \
    tar -xzf "${dl}/llvm-cov.tgz" -C /usr/local/bin cargo-llvm-cov; \
    fetch deny.tgz "https://github.com/EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny/releases/download/${CARGO_DENY_VERSION}/cargo-deny-${CARGO_DENY_VERSION}-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz" "${CARGO_DENY_SHA256}"; \
    tar -xzf "${dl}/deny.tgz" -C /usr/local/bin --strip-components=1 "cargo-deny-${CARGO_DENY_VERSION}-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/cargo-deny"; \
    fetch tinymold.tgz "https://github.com/tinyhumansai/tinymold/releases/download/v${TINYMOLD_VERSION}/tinymold-${TINYMOLD_VERSION}-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz" "${TINYMOLD_SHA256}"; \
    mkdir "${dl}/tm"; tar -xzf "${dl}/tinymold.tgz" -C "${dl}/tm"; \
    install -m 0755 "$(find "${dl}/tm" -type f -name tinymold | head -n1)" /usr/local/bin/tinymold; \
    rm -rf "${dl}"

# Fail the build, not a CI job, when something above is missing.
RUN rustc +stable --version && rustc "+${RUST_MSRV}" --version && cargo clippy --version \
    && rustc "+${RUST_NIGHTLY}" -Zcodegen-backend=cranelift --version \
    && cargo fmt --version && cargo llvm-cov --version && cargo deny --version \
    && tinymold --version && mongod --version | head -1 && mongosh --version \
    && mold --version && jq --version

# TinyHumans module CI contract

Module repositories call the reusable workflow at
`.github/workflows/module-ci.yml` in `tinyhumansai/.github`. The workflow
publishes the same required check names in every caller:

- `fmt`
- `clippy`
- `test`
- `coverage`
- `docs`
- `msrv`
- `supply-chain`
- `module-e2e (ubuntu-latest)`, `module-e2e (macos-latest)`,
  `module-e2e (windows-latest)`
- `feature-tests (ubuntu-latest)`, `feature-tests (macos-latest)`,
  `feature-tests (windows-latest)`

Each module owns its test commands and platform dependencies. The workflow
caller supplies repository-relative Bash scripts for its coverage gate, loader
suite, and feature suite, and any Ubuntu packages needed
to build or test it. The shared workflow validates those script paths before
running them. The `test` job runs
the default feature set; the feature-test script runs on all three operating
systems. The MSRV job and each module-e2e runner read `rust-version` from Cargo
metadata. For a concrete workspace, the root package declaration remains
authoritative. For a virtual workspace, the workflow selects the numerically
highest declared `rust-version` among workspace members, excluding external
dependencies. Missing declarations and malformed version strings fail the
selection instead of silently choosing a compiler. This keeps the compiler
selection aligned with the workspace rather than OS path spelling. The legacy `msrv` input is
optional and ignored while existing callers migrate. `msrv-build-targets` can
provide validated Cargo build groups when a repository deliberately supports
an older compiler for its public libraries than for optional or unpublished
workspace crates. Its JSON specifies only package names, feature lists, and
build flags, not shell commands. The check still installs the root package's
declared `rust-version`. `module-e2e-toolchain` defaults to `declared`; set it
to `stable` for the latest stable compiler, or to an exact `X.Y.Z` release such
as `1.88.0` when it needs a reproducible compiler newer than the public library
MSRV. A caller is ready to become a required-check ruleset
target only after every supplied command succeeds on its target runners.

## Release callers

Release callers use `module-release.yml` with the existing release tag and
version, the module cdylib package name, extra package files, the distro toggle,
and the crates.io toggle/package. The shared pipeline builds and verifies the
same 11 native targets in every repository. With distro builds enabled, it also
builds Fedora 43/44 and Arch on x86_64 and arm64, for 17 archives total.

The per-repository scripts implement this interface:

- `scripts/build-module.sh` and `scripts/build-module.ps1` accept `--crate`,
  `--version`, `--target`, `--host`, `--extra-files-json`, and `--output-dir`
  (PowerShell uses `-Crate`, `-Version`, `-Target`, `-HostKey`,
  `-ExtraFilesJson`, and `-OutputDir`). They emit exactly one archive named
  `<crate>-<version>-<host>.tar.gz` or `.zip`, containing the library and its
  `modules.toml` digest.
- `scripts/verify-module.sh` and `scripts/verify-module.ps1` accept `--archive`
  / `-Archive` and load the artifact through TinyBus, exercising the module's
  members.
- `scripts/test-distro.sh` accepts the image followed by the same build inputs;
  it builds and verifies inside that distro image and writes the same archive
  into the output directory.

The release workflow refuses to publish unless it collected exactly 11 native
archives, or all 17 archives when distro builds are enabled. It creates
`checksum.toml` with TinyBus and creates the release once; it does not update an
existing release. Each caller repository must have GitHub immutable releases
enabled; GitHub enforces immutability on publication. Debian and Ubuntu are
represented by the Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 native builds, which already exercise
their LTS glibc baselines. Alpine/musl is not included because TinyBus currently
selects no module artifact for musl hosts. FreeBSD is outside the shipped
Windows/macOS/Linux product set.

When crates.io publishing is enabled, the workflow first dry-runs the package
from the tag, then publishes it after the GitHub release is created. A failed
publish can be retried safely: the workflow recognizes an already-published
crate version and skips it.

Do not rename or remove a required job in the shared workflow without updating
the organization ruleset and the shared drift check in the same change.

## Version changes and SDK releases

Version changes land through a PR before a vX.Y.Z tag is created at the merged
commit. Module release callers accept an existing tag; they never push a bump
commit to main. The shared pipeline verifies that the tagged commit is an
ancestor of main before building.

TinyBus owns the loader/runtime SDK and has no loadable cdylib. It calls the
shared sdk-release.yml to publish a source archive and checksum.toml. Native
module archives and module-load verification are not applicable to that SDK;
its three-platform loader fixture tests remain required CI checks.

## Drift detection

The shared repository's CI runs offline regression tests on every PR. On every
push, manual dispatch, and daily schedule, the module-drift job reads the public
main workflows and active rulesets of all 13 upstream repositories. API errors
fail the job rather than silently skipping a repository. It checks canonical
callers pinned to commit SHAs, all 17 release targets (with the documented
TinyBus SDK exception), the 13 Actions check contexts, strict up-to-date main
protection, required PRs and resolved review threads, deletion/force-push
protection. GitHub hides bypass actors from the default CI token; the audit
prints that limitation. With administrator credentials locally, it additionally
checks administrator bypass on every active branch ruleset. Visible bypass
metadata that violates the contract always fails.

Run locally with Python and PyYAML 6.0.3:

```sh
python3 scripts/test-module-drift.py
GH_TOKEN="$(gh auth token)" python3 scripts/check-module-drift.py
```

This verifies the workflow and ruleset contract. Each module remains responsible
for the behavior and completeness of its scenario and module member tests.

Documented supplemental jobs remain allowed: TinyWallet dependency boundaries,
TinyComputer published-artifact verification, and TinyDocs source packaging.
They supplement the shared checks and release rather than replacing them.

          MODULE_CRATE: ${{ inputs.module-crate }}
          MODULE_ASSET: ${{ inputs.asset-name || inputs.module-crate }}
          EXTRA_PACKAGED_FILES: ${{ inputs.extra-packaged-files }}
          PUBLISH_CRATES_IO: ${{ inputs.publish-crates-io }}
          MODULE_MANIFEST: ${{ inputs.module-manifest }}
          CRATES_IO_PACKAGE: ${{ inputs.crates-io-package }}
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ ! "$VERSION" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([+-][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
            echo "version must be a semver version without a leading v" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          [[ "$MODULE_ASSET" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ ]] || { echo "invalid asset-name" >&2; exit 2; }
          if [[ ! "$MODULE_CRATE" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ ]]; then
            echo "module-crate must be a Cargo package name" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! jq -e 'type == "array" and all(.[]; type == "string")' <<<"$EXTRA_PACKAGED_FILES" >/dev/null; then
            echo "extra-packaged-files must be a JSON array of strings" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "$PUBLISH_CRATES_IO" == "true" ]]; then
            if [[ -z "$CRATES_IO_PACKAGE" || -z "$CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN" ]]; then
              echo "crates-io-package and CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN are required when publishing to crates.io" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          fi
      - name: Require packaging scripts at the tagged revision
        shell: bash
        env:
          INCLUDE_DISTROS: ${{ inputs.include-distros }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          required=(scripts/build-module.sh scripts/build-module.ps1 scripts/verify-module.sh scripts/verify-module.ps1)
          if [[ "$INCLUDE_DISTROS" == "true" ]]; then required+=(scripts/test-distro.sh); fi
          for script in "${required[@]}"; do
            if [[ ! -f "$script" ]]; then
              echo "release tag does not contain required packaging script: $script" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          for script in scripts/build-module.sh scripts/verify-module.sh; do
            if [[ ! -x "$script" ]]; then
              echo "release tag packaging script is not executable: $script" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          if [[ "$INCLUDE_DISTROS" == "true" && ! -x scripts/test-distro.sh ]]; then
            echo "release tag packaging script is not executable: scripts/test-distro.sh" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
      - name: Match requested version to Cargo packages at the tag
        shell: bash
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          MODULE_CRATE: ${{ inputs.module-crate }}
          MODULE_ASSET: ${{ inputs.asset-name || inputs.module-crate }}
          MODULE_MANIFEST: ${{ inputs.module-manifest }}
          PUBLISH_CRATES_IO: ${{ inputs.publish-crates-io }}
          CRATES_IO_PACKAGE: ${{ inputs.crates-io-package }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          [[ "$MODULE_MANIFEST" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+Cargo.toml$ || "$MODULE_MANIFEST" == Cargo.toml ]] &&
            [[ "$MODULE_MANIFEST" != /* && "$MODULE_MANIFEST" != ../* && "$MODULE_MANIFEST" != */../* ]] || {
            echo "module-manifest must be a repository-relative Cargo.toml path" >&2
            exit 2
          }
          metadata=$(cargo metadata --manifest-path "$MODULE_MANIFEST" --format-version 1 --no-deps)
          module_version=$(jq -r --arg name "$MODULE_CRATE" \
            '[.packages[] | select(.name == $name) | .version] | if length == 1 then .[0] else "" end' \
            <<<"$metadata")
          if [[ "$module_version" != "$VERSION" ]]; then
            echo "module crate $MODULE_CRATE is version ${module_version:-missing}, expected $VERSION" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "$PUBLISH_CRATES_IO" == "true" ]]; then
            registry_version=$(jq -r --arg name "$CRATES_IO_PACKAGE" \
              '[.packages[] | select(.name == $name) | .version] | if length == 1 then .[0] else "" end' \
              <<<"$metadata")
            if [[ "$registry_version" != "$VERSION" ]]; then
              echo "crates.io package $CRATES_IO_PACKAGE is version ${registry_version:-missing}, expected $VERSION" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Initialise the submodules of the repository at $1, shallow and in parallel,
# leaving out every submodule whose path matches an EXCLUDE pattern.
#
# Environment (all optional):
#   EXCLUDE    newline-separated globs over the path from the root; `*` also
#              matches `/`, and a pattern without `/` matches the last path
#              component at any depth (default: none)
#   RECURSIVE  `true` descends into submodules of submodules (default: true)
#   DEPTH      history depth of each submodule; 0 = full (default: 1)
#   JOBS       submodules cloned at once (default: 8)
#   TOKEN      sent to github.com as an HTTP header for this process only,
#              never written to any git config
#
# Submodules are added a level at a time: every parent of a level runs its
# `git submodule update` at once, each cloning up to JOBS submodules, and the
# submodules it added become the next level's parents. An excluded submodule
# stays an empty directory, and nothing beneath it is visited.
set -euo pipefail

root="$(cd "${1:?usage: $0 <repository dir>}" && pwd)"
recursive="${RECURSIVE:-true}"
depth="${DEPTH:-1}"
jobs="${JOBS:-8}"

patterns=()
while IFS= read -r line; do
	line="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
	line="${line%"${line##*[![:space:]]}"}"
	[[ -n "${line}" ]] && patterns+=("${line}")
done <<<"${EXCLUDE:-}"

# Config for every git the updates spawn, through the environment so that it
# is gone when this script exits. In a container job the workspace belongs to
# the runner's user but git runs as root, so git refuses every repository in
# it as unsafe unless safe.directory says otherwise; actions/checkout does the
# same for its own calls.
export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1
export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0="safe.directory"
export GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0="*"
if [[ -n "${TOKEN:-}" ]]; then
	basic="$(printf 'x-access-token:%s' "${TOKEN}" | base64 | tr -d '\n')"
	echo "::add-mask::${basic}"
	export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=2
	export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1="http.https://github.com/.extraheader"
	export GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1="AUTHORIZATION: basic ${basic}"
fi

excluded() {
	local rel="$1" pattern
	for pattern in "${patterns[@]+"${patterns[@]}"}"; do
		if [[ "${pattern}" == */* ]]; then
			# shellcheck disable=SC2053  # the pattern is a glob on purpose
			[[ "${rel}" == ${pattern} ]] && return 0
		else
			# shellcheck disable=SC2053
			[[ "${rel##*/}" == ${pattern} ]] && return 0
		fi
	done
	return 1
}

# update <parent rel> <submodule path>...: clone the given submodules of one
# parent, at the commits it records.
update() {
	local parent="$1"
	shift
	local args=(submodule update --init --jobs "${jobs}")
	((depth > 0)) && args+=(--depth "${depth}")
	git -C "${root}/${parent}" "${args[@]}" -- "$@"
}

level=(.)
total=0
skipped=0
while ((${#level[@]})); do
	next=()
	pids=()
	for parent in "${level[@]}"; do
		dir="${root}/${parent}"
		[[ -f "${dir}/.gitmodules" ]] || continue
		wanted=()
		while read -r _ path; do
			rel="${path}"
			[[ "${parent}" != . ]] && rel="${parent}/${path}"
			if excluded "${rel}"; then
				echo "skip ${rel}"
				skipped=$((skipped + 1))
			else
				wanted+=("${path}")
				next+=("${rel}")
			fi
		done < <(git -C "${dir}" config --file .gitmodules --get-regexp '^submodule\..*\.path$' || true)
		((${#wanted[@]})) || continue
		total=$((total + ${#wanted[@]}))
		update "${parent}" "${wanted[@]}" &
		pids+=($!)
	done
	for pid in "${pids[@]+"${pids[@]}"}"; do
		wait "${pid}"
	done
	[[ "${recursive}" == true ]] || break
	level=("${next[@]+"${next[@]}"}")
done

echo "checked out ${total} submodules, skipped ${skipped}"

# Check a repository out with its submodules, minus the ones a build never
# reads. actions/checkout clones every submodule one after another; this
# checks the repository out without them, then adds them shallow, a level at a
# time and in parallel, skipping every path that matches `exclude-submodules`
# (the wiki submodules, by default). See README.md beside this file.
name: Checkout (selective submodules)
description: actions/checkout, then shallow parallel submodules that skip excluded paths such as wikis.

inputs:
  ref:
    description: The branch, tag or SHA to check out; defaults to the event's ref.
    default: ""
  path:
    description: Where to check the repository out, relative to the workspace.
    default: ""
  token:
    [REDACTED] Token for the repository and any github.com submodule; never written to git config unless persist-credentials is true.
    default: ${{ github.token }}
  persist-credentials:
    description: Whether actions/checkout leaves the token in the repository's git config.
    default: "false"
  fetch-depth:
    description: History depth of the repository itself (0 = all history).
    default: "1"
  sparse-checkout:
    description: Passed to actions/checkout, for skipping directories of the repository itself.
    default: ""
  submodules:
    description: "`recursive` (every level), `true` (the first level only) or `false`."
    default: recursive
  exclude-submodules:
    description: >-
      Newline-separated globs of submodule paths to leave out, matched against
      the path from the repository root. `*` also matches `/`, and a pattern
      without a `/` matches the last path component at any depth, so `wiki`
      leaves out every submodule called wiki.
    default: wiki
  submodule-depth:
    description: History depth of each submodule.
    default: "1"
  jobs:
    description: How many submodules to clone at once.
    default: "8"

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262
      with:
        ref: ${{ inputs.ref }}
        path: ${{ inputs.path }}
        token: ${{ inputs.token }}
        persist-credentials: ${{ inputs.persist-credentials }}
        fetch-depth: ${{ inputs.fetch-depth }}
        sparse-checkout: ${{ inputs.sparse-checkout }}
        submodules: false

    - if: inputs.submodules != 'false'
      shell: bash
      env:
        REPO_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/${{ inputs.path }}
        RECURSIVE: ${{ inputs.submodules == 'recursive' }}
        EXCLUDE: ${{ inputs.exclude-submodules }}
        DEPTH: ${{ inputs.submodule-depth }}
        JOBS: ${{ inputs.jobs }}
        TOKEN: ${{ inputs.token }}
      run: '"${GITHUB_ACTION_PATH}/checkout-submodules.sh" "${REPO_DIR}"'

"""Exercise the MSRV selection shared by both module CI jobs."""

import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
import subprocess
import unittest
import os
import tempfile


WORKFLOW = Path(__file__).parents[1] / ".github/workflows/module-ci.yml"


class WorkspaceMsrvTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def queries(self):
        workflow = WORKFLOW.read_text()
        queries = re.findall(r"jq -er '(.*?)'", workflow, re.S)
        self.assertEqual(len(queries), 2)
        return queries

    def select(self, metadata):
        results = [
            subprocess.run(
                ["jq", "-er", query],
                input=json.dumps(metadata),
                text=True,
                capture_output=True,
                check=False,
            )
            for query in self.queries()
        ]
        return results

    def test_concrete_workspace_keeps_root_package_msrv(self):
        metadata = {
            "workspace_members": ["root", "member"],
            "packages": [
                {"id": "root", "rust_version": "1.85"},
                {"id": "member", "rust_version": "1.100"},
                {"id": "dependency", "rust_version": "1.120"},
            ],
            "resolve": {"root": "root"},
        }
        results = self.select(metadata)
        self.assertEqual([result.returncode for result in results], [0, 0])
        self.assertEqual([result.stdout.strip() for result in results], ["1.85", "1.85"])

    def test_virtual_workspace_uses_highest_member_msrv_numerically(self):
        metadata = {
            "workspace_members": ["older", "newer"],
            "packages": [
                {"id": "older", "rust_version": "1.99"},
                {"id": "newer", "rust_version": "1.100"},
                {"id": "dependency", "rust_version": "1.200"},
            ],
            "resolve": {"root": None},
        }
        results = self.select(metadata)
        self.assertEqual([result.returncode for result in results], [0, 0])
        self.assertEqual([result.stdout.strip() for result in results], ["1.100", "1.100"])

    def test_virtual_workspace_without_declared_member_msrv_is_rejected(self):
        metadata = {
            "workspace_members": ["one", "two"],
            "packages": [
                {"id": "one", "rust_version": None},
                {"id": "two", "rust_version": None},
                {"id": "dependency", "rust_version": "1.88"},
            ],
            "resolve": {"root": None},
        }
        for result in self.select(metadata):
            self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0)
            self.assertIn("workspace members must declare rust-version", result.stderr)

    def test_concrete_root_without_msrv_is_rejected(self):
        metadata = {
            "workspace_members": ["root", "member"],
            "packages": [
                {"id": "root", "rust_version": None},
                {"id": "member", "rust_version": "1.88"},
            ],
            "resolve": {"root": "root"},
        }
        for result in self.select(metadata):
            self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0)
            self.assertIn("workspace root package must declare rust-version", result.stderr)

    def test_malformed_concrete_root_msrv_is_rejected(self):
        metadata = {
            "workspace_members": ["root"],
            "packages": [{"id": "root", "rust_version": "stable"}],
            "resolve": {"root": "root"},
        }
        for result in self.select(metadata):
            self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0)
            self.assertIn("workspace root rust-version must be numeric X.Y or X.Y.Z", result.stderr)

    def test_malformed_workspace_member_msrv_is_rejected(self):
        metadata = {
            "workspace_members": ["one", "two"],
            "packages": [
                {"id": "one", "rust_version": "stable"},
                {"id": "two", "rust_version": "1.88"},
            ],
            "resolve": {"root": None},
        }
        for result in self.select(metadata):
            self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0)
            self.assertIn("workspace package rust-version must be numeric X.Y or X.Y.Z", result.stderr)


    def test_selected_package_features_stay_with_their_own_package(self):
        """Each public package builds at its compiler with only its qualified features."""
        workflow = (Path(__file__).parents[1] / ".github/workflows/module-ci.yml").read_text()
        block = workflow.split("      - name: Build with the declared MSRV", 1)[1]
        script = block.split("        run: |\n", 1)[1].split("\n  supply-chain:", 1)[0]
        script = "\n".join(line[10:] for line in script.splitlines())
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            root = Path(directory)
            log = root / "calls"
            metadata = {"packages": [{"name": "a", "rust_version": "1.70", "features": {"foo": []}},
                                     {"name": "b", "rust_version": "1.88", "features": {"bar": []}}]}
            cargo = root / "cargo"
            cargo.write_text("#!/usr/bin/env python3\nimport json,sys\n"
                             "if 'metadata' in sys.argv: print(" + repr(json.dumps(metadata)) + ")\n"
                             "else:\n"
                             " with open(" + repr(str(log)) + ", 'a') as f: f.write(json.dumps(sys.argv[1:])+'\\n')\n")
            cargo.chmod(0o755)
            rustup = root / "rustup"; rustup.write_text("#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n"); rustup.chmod(0o755)
            env = dict(os.environ, PATH=str(root)+os.pathsep+os.environ["PATH"],
                       MSRV_BUILD_TARGETS=json.dumps([{"packages":["a","b"],"features":["a/foo","b/bar","foo"]}]))
            result = subprocess.run(["bash","-e","-o","pipefail","-c",script], env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
            self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
            calls = [json.loads(line) for line in log.read_text().splitlines()]
            self.assertEqual(calls, [["+1.70","build","--package","a","--features","a/foo","--features","foo"],
                                     ["+1.88","build","--package","b","--features","b/bar"]])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Offline regressions for actions/checkout/checkout-submodules.sh.

Builds a superproject with nested submodules (and wiki submodules at several
depths) from local repositories, then checks which ones the script clones.
"""
import os
import pathlib
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

SCRIPT = pathlib.Path(__file__).parents[1] / "actions/checkout/checkout-submodules.sh"
ENV = {
    **os.environ,
    "GIT_AUTHOR_NAME": "t", "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL": "t@example.com",
    "GIT_COMMITTER_NAME": "t", "GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL": "t@example.com",
    "GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM": "1", "GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL": "file",
}


def git(cwd, *args):
    subprocess.run(["git", "-c", "protocol.file.allow=always", "-c", "init.defaultBranch=main", *args],
                   cwd=cwd, env=ENV, check=True, capture_output=True)


class CheckoutSubmodulesTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        base = pathlib.Path(self.tmp.name)
        self.home = base / "home"
        self.home.mkdir()
        ENV["HOME"] = str(self.home)
        self.origin = base / "origin"

        def repo(name, subs=()):
            path = self.origin / name
            path.mkdir(parents=True)
            git(path, "init", "-q")
            (path / "README").write_text(name)
            for sub, dest in subs:
                git(path, "submodule", "add", "-q", (self.origin / sub).as_uri(), dest)
            git(path, "add", "-A")
            git(path, "commit", "-q", "-m", name)

        repo("leaf")
        repo("wiki")
        repo("lib", [("leaf", "vendor/leaf"), ("wiki", "wiki")])
        repo("top", [("lib", "vendor/lib"), ("wiki", "wiki"), ("leaf", "docs/wiki-tools")])
        self.work = base / "work"
        git(base, "clone", "-q", (self.origin / "top").as_uri(), str(self.work))

    def tearDown(self):
        self.tmp.cleanup()

    def run_script(self, **env):
        result = subprocess.run([str(SCRIPT), str(self.work)], env={**ENV, **env}, text=True,
                                capture_output=True)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        return result.stdout

    def cloned(self, rel):
        return (self.work / rel / "README").is_file()

    def test_bare_name_skips_wikis_at_every_depth(self):
        out = self.run_script(EXCLUDE="wiki\n")
        self.assertTrue(self.cloned("vendor/lib"))
        self.assertTrue(self.cloned("vendor/lib/vendor/leaf"))
        self.assertTrue(self.cloned("docs/wiki-tools"))
        self.assertFalse(self.cloned("wiki"))
        self.assertFalse(self.cloned("vendor/lib/wiki"))
        self.assertIn("checked out 3 submodules, skipped 2", out)

    def test_path_pattern_matches_from_the_root(self):
        self.run_script(EXCLUDE="vendor/*/wiki")
        self.assertTrue(self.cloned("wiki"))
        self.assertFalse(self.cloned("vendor/lib/wiki"))

    def test_excluding_a_parent_skips_everything_beneath_it(self):
        out = self.run_script(EXCLUDE="vendor/lib")
        self.assertFalse(self.cloned("vendor/lib"))
        self.assertTrue(self.cloned("wiki"))
        self.assertNotIn("vendor/lib/", out)

    def test_non_recursive_stops_at_the_first_level(self):
        self.run_script(RECURSIVE="false")
        self.assertTrue(self.cloned("vendor/lib"))
        self.assertFalse(self.cloned("vendor/lib/vendor/leaf"))

    def test_no_exclusions_clones_everything(self):
        out = self.run_script()
        self.assertIn("checked out 5 submodules, skipped 0", out)

    def test_clones_are_shallow(self):
        self.run_script(DEPTH="1")
        shallow = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--is-shallow-repository"], cwd=self.work / "vendor/lib",
                                 env=ENV, text=True, capture_output=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
        self.assertEqual(shallow, "true")

    def test_token_never_reaches_git_config(self):
        self.run_script(TOKEN="[REDACTED]")
        for config in [self.work / ".git/config", *self.work.glob(".git/modules/**/config")]:
            self.assertNotIn("extraheader", config.read_text())

    def test_a_checkout_owned_by_another_user_still_gets_its_submodules(self):
        # A container job runs as root over a workspace the runner's user owns.
        # git's test hook makes every repository look foreign, as it does there.
        out = self.run_script(TOKEN="[REDACTED]", GIT_TEST_ASSUME_DIFFERENT_OWNER="1")
        self.assertTrue(self.cloned("vendor/lib/vendor/leaf"))
        self.assertIn("checked out 5 submodules", out)
        self.assertNotIn("safe.directory", (self.home / ".gitconfig").read_text()
                         if (self.home / ".gitconfig").exists() else "")

    def test_a_failed_clone_fails_the_script(self):
        (self.origin / "leaf").rename(self.origin / "gone")
        result = subprocess.run([str(SCRIPT), str(self.work)], env=ENV, capture_output=True)
        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Prove additional source packages cannot change verified module assets."""
import importlib.util
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
import unittest

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("source_assets", Path(__file__).with_name("merge-source-assets.py"))
module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(module)

class SourceAssetsTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_valid_flat_artifact_is_copied(self):
        """Flat source packages are appended to the release."""
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as root:
            source, dest = Path(root)/"source", Path(root)/"dest"
            source.mkdir(); dest.mkdir()
            (source/"sdk.crate").write_bytes(b"source")
            module.merge(source, dest)
            self.assertEqual((dest/"sdk.crate").read_bytes(), b"source")

    def test_collision_preserves_every_original_asset(self):
        """A source checksum or archive cannot replace a verified module asset."""
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as root:
            source, dest = Path(root)/"source", Path(root)/"dest"
            source.mkdir(); dest.mkdir()
            (source/"sdk.crate").write_bytes(b"source")
            (source/"checksum.toml").write_bytes(b"replacement")
            (dest/"checksum.toml").write_bytes(b"verified")
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError): module.merge(source, dest)
            self.assertEqual((dest/"checksum.toml").read_bytes(), b"verified")
            self.assertFalse((dest/"sdk.crate").exists())

    def test_nested_artifact_is_rejected(self):
        """Directories are rejected before any asset is copied."""
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as root:
            source, dest = Path(root)/"source", Path(root)/"dest"
            source.mkdir(); dest.mkdir(); (source/"nested").mkdir()
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError): module.merge(source, dest)

    def test_workflow_embeds_the_validated_merger(self):
        """Caller checkouts do not contain the shared repository's scripts."""
        script = Path(__file__).with_name("merge-source-assets.py").read_text()
        workflow = (Path(__file__).parents[1]/".github/workflows/module-release.yml").read_text()
        self.assertIn("".join("          "+line+"\n" for line in script.splitlines()), workflow)

if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()
